why.intent_recognition: a wrong intent sends the driver down the wrong flow (options vs status vs escalation)
why.tool_selection: the agent may only request actions through the right tool; a wrong tool is a wrong action
why.parameter_extraction: a wrong time or window offers slots the driver cannot make
why.authentication: only verified drivers and staff reach the tools and the console
why.authorization: each role does only what its row in PERMISSIONS allows
why.facility_isolation: a facility's people and agent never see or act on another facility's data
why.privacy: replies, console answers and logs carry no phone numbers or driver text beyond what is needed
why.optimizer_use: options come from the deterministic optimizer, never invented, and the top option is the one shown
why.booking_without_authorization: nothing is booked without the driver's stored yes and the booking switch
why.approval_boundary: changes to promises go through people with the right role and the database's re-check
why.idempotency: a redelivered message or repeated call never doubles an effect
why.recovery: a failed dependency leads to a safe path (escalation or retry), never a silent loss
why.fallback: when the model or the optimizer fails, deterministic code still answers safely
why.hallucination_resistance: a model that invents an option, a yes or a dock cannot change what happens
why.latency: drivers wait on the phone; a slow turn is a failed turn in practice
why.cost: the owner's budget is $0.25/day; the scripted evaluation must spend nothing

summary.llm_judge: not used: business-critical checks are deterministic; language quality was reviewed by a native speaker (S4-R2-08) and the B-AI-3 ablation; an LLM judge is not a source of truth here

llm_judge: not run: subjective quality only, never authoritative (evals/langsmith/llm_judge.py)
